in_text_mentions: In the microscopic image, characteristic lymphoid cells, so-called hairy cells, are observed (Figure 3). Hairy cells have a diameter of 10 to 25 µm, a round, oval, or bean-shaped cell nucleus with sparse chromatin, and abundant, pale blue and jagged cytoplasm with shaggy projections. Occasionally, fine granules may be found (9, 10, 18, 24). panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (clinical_photo_left, clinical_photo_right, a, b, c, d). clinical_photo_left: Clinical photograph shows extensive erythematous-to-violaceous maculopapular lesions on the hands, forearms, and lower extremities, explicitly attributed in the caption to cutaneous leukocytoclastic vasculitis associated with HCL. clinical_photo_right: Clinical photograph shows a diffuse erythematous-to-violaceous maculopapular eruption on the arm and trunk, explicitly captioned as cutaneous leukocytoclastic vasculitis at HCL diagnosis. a: Panel a is an H&E skin biopsy from the eruption, showing vascular and inflammatory changes explicitly described in the caption as granulocytic and lymphocytic inflammation in subcutaneous small and large vessels. b: Panel b is a higher-magnification H&E skin biopsy section demonstrating the inflammatory vascular process attributed to cutaneous leukocytoclastic vasculitis in HCL. c: Panel c directly shows the characteristic histopathology...
panels.attribution_text: Robak et al. Skin changes in hairy cell leukemia.. Annals of hematology 2021. doi:10.1007/s00277-020-04349-z. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Maculopapular skin rash due to paraneoplastic dermatitis with cutaneous leukocytoclastic vasculitis on upper and lower extremities at diagnosis of HCL. Similar lesions were present on the chest, back, and neck. Skin biopsy with granulocytic and lymphocytic inflammation in small and large vessels in subcutaneous tissue (a, b, c) (HE × 20, × 100, × 200); fibrinoid necrosis and leukocytoclasis (fragmented neutrophilic nuclei) (c) with destruction of vessel wall (immunohistochemical staining for desmin, DAKO, × 200) (d)

Vasculitis with skin erythema can be an initial manifestation of early-stage HCL [67, 70]; it can also precede the clinical manifestations of HCL or follow a diagnosis of HCL (Fig. 1) [67, 69, 71, 72]. Although the pathogenesis of vasculitis is unknown, it is believed that immune complex injury and cross-reactions between autoantibodies to hairy cells and endothelial cells may take part [68, 69, 73].
